summer.body:
Planting tickets: 
majority of planting tickets seem to have gone well, a few callbacks for planting depth and concerns. definitely more people needing trees staked then usual it felt like. 
Tropicals- 
They seemed to move pretty well, with lots of positive feedback about that fill a cart sale. 
Hanging baskets moved decently quickly at first then slowed way down in my opinion. 
-Powdery mildew in the perennial house at times. 
- ran out of burlap for wrapping trees. 
-felt like I was spraying for aphids almost every week on the tropicals
-welded pots have been a good addition

Jacob - Summer Notes 2026. Successful in getting the varieties of bulbs I wanted by placing order even earlier. June 1 it should be done, if not earlier. Make it clear to ship what is available by end of August – it’s September 5th today and we still don’t have any bulbs, but we were invoiced yesterday. Garlic arrived last week, looks good. The ‘fill a cart’ sale that included donating the proceeds was a big success, it seems. I think customers like the chance to feel like they’re giving back
We sold out of potting soil fairly early which was a drop ship, and I’ve had to order two more pallets
Only did a couple of houseplant orders during the slow time which was plenty
It was really beneficial to have the professionals come and clean upstairs after the spring season
First round of stacker pumpkins delivered fri. Sept. 3/Labor Day weekend

Summer 2026 Notes
We had a pretty good summer overall weather wise. Very good rains until late August when it dried up. Some very warm days, ie July 4 and late August. We were overstaffed most days and per usual, the people we kept on all summer have now left once Fall started getting busy again (mostly college kids). We need to running on a slimmer crew with people who can run the register and work on the yard both so we dont have to have as many people. Lots of twiddling thumbs and sitting around at the front/potting table. How can we add more summer things/activities? It’s almost like having something to do that just breaks even is better than having bored/disappointed employees for 2 months. It just seemed to be a longer summer than usual, but I’m sure they all seem that way in the moment. What experience things - coffee? Food trucks? Kids gardening, Little Kentucky Gardeners Club on Saturday’s? Just something to keep the energy going here in the summer so it’s not just dragging.

I thought sales would have been better with more moisture out there but it didn’t seem to be true. I guess only lack of rain hurts and not the opposite. We had several weeks with no planters or deliveries. The deck collapsed this summer and will be rebuilt sometime in September. We also had a plumbing issue that required replacing the old cast iron pipes in the floor - from the downstairs bathroom, thru the sink closet, thru the water heater closet and out under the deck - done by Medyna Plumbing sometime in September.

See sales and trucks incoming on the Github calendar. We decorated big for July 4 this year - stars in grass, big flags in greenhouse, flags from front porch, special shirts for staff. We did a couple disposable cameras in late Spring and Summer, lots of fun. Russ, Jonathan, Brooke and I did Cultivate for one day - worth the trip to see some new stuff and say some hellos. Ben, Russ and I did the zoo trial gardens in Cincy one day, worth it.
